name: STANDALONE
positive_standard: Source states or exemplifies the specified use constituting an utterance on its own as a conventional use
negative_standard: Source states the use cannot constitute an utterance alone in this use, or is bound to a host
notes: Solitary occurrence, an answer fragment, or contextual dependence alone does not support Y; record them in notes Family POSITION (P01-P03): N on all three is impossible, since a use occurs somewhere; 'standalone only' (P01 Y, P02 N, P03 N) is a derived joint state, not coded.
claim: may constitute an utterance on its own as a conventional use

name: SUPPLEMENT
positive_standard: Source states or exemplifies the use beside a complete clause without entering its construction
negative_standard: Source states the use never occurs beside a complete clause without entering its construction, with the supplement environment addressed. A statement that the use is always integrated or always standalone supports this N and the matching P01 or P03 value as one proposition (dependence state: entailed)
notes: Calibration: Ameka co-utterances in their distributional context; source wording preserved Family POSITION (P01-P03): N on all three is impossible, since a use occurs somewhere; 'standalone only' (P01 Y, P02 N, P03 N) is a derived joint state, not coded.
claim: may occur beside a complete clause without entering its construction

name: INTEGRATED
positive_standard: Source states or exemplifies the use in an argument, complement, or modifier position
negative_standard: Source restricts the use to standalone and/or supplement positions
notes: An N is an absence and carries a strength field: stated / opportunity-documented / both Family POSITION (P01-P03): N on all three is impossible, since a use occurs somewhere; 'standalone only' (P01 Y, P02 N, P03 N) is a derived joint state, not coded.
claim: may occur in an argument, complement, or modifier position

name: DEPENDENTS
positive_standard: Source states or exemplifies the use taking a complement or modifier (determiners excluded; see P06)
negative_standard: Source states the use takes no complements or modifiers
notes: A statement covering all dependents supports P04 and P06 separately, with dependence state entailed between them
claim: may take a complement or modifier

name: INFLECTS
positive_standard: Source gives an inflected form of the specified use (number excluded; see P06)
negative_standard: Source states invariance, or gives a paradigm covering the relevant contrasts and shows one form
corpus_N_opportunity: Contexts in which a rival verb or adjective analysis would require an inflected form (past time, third singular present, comparative frame); N at K or more such opportunities with no inflected form
notes: Derivation is recorded separately and does not count as inflection
claim: may occur in an inflected form (number excluded)

name: NOMINAL_COMB
positive_standard: Source or attested line shows the use with a determiner (including quantifying determinatives) or in plural form; the cell records which disjunct supports Y (determiner / plural)
negative_standard: Explicit unacceptability statement for the specified use. A conversion analysis is contrast evidence: U in the primary record, N only in a predeclared sensitivity, as for P08
corpus_N_opportunity: Occurrences heading a phrase in an argument or predicative position where a count noun would take a determiner or plural; N at K or more with none
notes: Record attested combinations separately from any conversion analysis; sign-type identity is not revised because an adverse combination appears Disjunctive, kept whole because it is a shared target.
claim: may occur with a determiner or in plural form

name: NONPROP
positive_standard: Source states the use makes no contribution to descriptive or truth-conditional content
negative_standard: Source assigns ordinary descriptive or truth-conditional content to the use
notes: Shared diagnostic of INTJ and EXPRESSIVE; both groupings have a no-P07 sensitivity Superseded 2026-11-05: its Y is a never-claim. Recoded as P07D with values reversed (old Y = P07D N; old N = P07D Y), which converts mechanically.

name: DESCRIPTIVE
positive_standard: Source assigns ordinary descriptive or truth-conditional content to the specified use (one admissible instance)
negative_standard: Source states the use makes no contribution to descriptive or truth-conditional content
notes: Possibility form of P07, values reversed; its sign is negative for both groupings. Shared diagnostic of INTJ and EXPRESSIVE; both keep a no-P07 sensitivity. Mixed items are Y (Gutzmann 2013, p. 10, intensifier fucking).
claim: may contribute descriptive or truth-conditional content

name: STANCE
positive_standard: Span states evaluative or affective content for the specified use or for a class whose stated content is evaluative or affective; the word expressive or emotive alone does not support Y
negative_standard: Source excludes an evaluative or affective component for the use. Placement in a different descriptive class is contrast evidence: U in the primary record, N only in a predeclared sensitivity
notes: CGEL 1361 uses expressive in a broad non-propositional sense covering conative sh and hey
claim: may convey evaluative or affective content

name: DEPICTIVE
positive_standard: Source characterizes the use as depicting through resemblance between performance and what is depicted
negative_standard: Source states the use doesn't depict through resemblance (a statement that it is non-iconic counts)
claim: may depict through resemblance between performance and what is depicted

name: REPETITION_STRENGTHENS
positive_standard: Source states or exemplifies that the specified repetition pattern of the use strengthens the same contribution
negative_standard: Source states repetition in the pattern never strengthens the contribution (for example, is redundant)
corpus_N_opportunity: not available (an attested repetition does not show its effect)
notes: Pattern recorded: adjacent repetition / distributed recurrence / lengthening / lexicalized reduplication, with positions; Potts accumulated damn tokens are distributed recurrence across uses N narrowed 2026-11-05: unavailability is now x through P10A, not N (FREEZE section 6, P10: four evidence fields).
claim: may strengthen the same contribution when repeated in the pattern
x_when: P10A = N for the pattern (repetition unavailable)

name: REPETITION_MULTIPLIES
positive_standard: Source states repetition multiplies depicted events
negative_standard: Source states repetition does not multiply depicted events
notes: DEPICTIVE projection; outside v1
claim: may multiply depicted events when repeated in the pattern

name: REPEATABLE
positive_standard: Source states or exemplifies the use repeated in the specified pattern
negative_standard: Source states the pattern is unavailable for the use
notes: Gate for P10S, P10M and P10R: where P10A = N for a pattern, they are x for it. Pattern recorded as for P10S.
claim: may be repeated in the pattern

name: REPETITION_REDUNDANT
positive_standard: Source states or exemplifies repetition of the use in the pattern adding nothing (redundant)
negative_standard: Source states repetition in the pattern is never redundant
notes: FREEZE section 6, P10: more than one of strengthening, multiplication and redundancy may be supported.
claim: may be repeated in the pattern with no added effect

name: NEGATION_SURVIVES
positive_standard: Source states or exemplifies the specified contribution not interpreted in the scope of negation of a host clause
negative_standard: Source reports the contribution cancelled or embedded under negation of the host
corpus_N_opportunity: not available (scope is not readable from a line)
notes: Host relation recorded: integrated / external co-utterance / independent adjacent turn. INAPPLICABLE for uses with no host requires a checked eligibility record; it is not U Superseded 2026-11-05: Y needed one wide-scope example, which gives no 'never', and Y and N could both hold of one use. Recoded as P11E. Not convertible mechanically: old N becomes P11E Y; old Y becomes U unless the source states the wide reading is forced.

name: EMBEDDABLE_UNDER_NEGATION
positive_standard: Source states or exemplifies the specified contribution interpreted inside the scope of negation of a host clause (one admissible reading)
negative_standard: Source states the contribution is never interpreted in the scope of host negation: the wide reading is forced (Potts 2007, p. 172)
notes: Replaces P11N. N is the expressive value, so its sign is negative for EXPRESSIVE. Host relation recorded: integrated / external co-utterance / independent adjacent turn. Whether an independent adjacent turn counts as a host is open for Brett (FREEZE section 13).
claim: may be interpreted inside the scope of host negation
x_when: no host environment of any recorded relation; derived from the host record and the POSITION family, never coded

name: PROSODY_HOSTED
positive_standard: Source reports, or audio shows, a separate intonation unit when the use occurs with a host
negative_standard: Source reports, or audio shows, characteristic intonational integration with a host
corpus_N_opportunity: Audio-measured hosted tokens (boundary by pause or pitch reset); N at K or more hosted tokens integrated. Transcript punctuation alone counts for neither value
notes: A standalone utterance boundary is not the target observation Superseded 2026-11-05: N ('characteristic integration') was a typical-case claim, not 'never'. Recoded as P12S (the hosted target) and P12I.

name: PROSODY_SEPARATE
positive_standard: Source reports, or audio shows, a separate intonation unit when the use occurs with a host
negative_standard: Source states, or audio across the use's hosted occurrences shows, that it is never set off intonationally when hosted
notes: Replaces P12 as the hosted-prosody target. A standalone utterance boundary is not the target observation.
claim: may form a separate intonation unit when hosted

name: PROSODY_INTEGRATED
positive_standard: Source reports, or audio shows, intonational integration with a host
negative_standard: Source states the use is never intonationally integrated when hosted
notes: With P12S, gives three joint states: always separate, always integrated, either.
claim: may be intonationally integrated with a host

name: PHONO_ANOM
positive_standard: Source gives a conventional form with sounds outside ordinary English word phonology for the stated speech community
negative_standard: Source gives the conventional form(s) in full and all are within ordinary word phonology for that community
notes: Distinguish a permitted variant from evidence excluding all such variants
claim: may have a conventional form with sounds outside ordinary English word phonology
